headline: High: Flowise’s broad filesystem/network defaults can leak or corrupt Botpress-driven workflows; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared files and tool outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is an LLM chatbot platform and Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder with file and API tool surfaces. If Flowise writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or outputs that Botpress later ingests, instructions can be smuggled across the pair. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Flowise outputs are copied into Botpress prompts or knowledge files without sanitization
IF both agents share a writable workspace or uploaded file store
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Flowise outputs into Botpress prompts
Separate workspaces and uploaded-file directories
Add content provenance labels to all inter-agent artifacts
Require manual review before Botpress consumes Flowise-generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise explicitly reads and writes server filesystem files and sends data to model providers and configured HTTP/search tools; Botpress is a customer-support agent that may process sensitive conversations. If they share files or a datastore, Botpress content can be exfiltrated through Flowise’s broad egress. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Botpress conversation data is stored in a directory Flowise can read
IF Flowise flows send shared file contents to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Place Botpress and Flowise on separate hosts or containers
Restrict Flowise file access to a dedicated non-sensitive directory
Block Flowise egress except to approved endpoints
Redact customer-support transcripts before any Flowise ingestion
Audit shared storage permissions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Flowise can read and write the server filesystem and supports multiple instances with shared datastore state. Even without shell access, overlapping writes to shared files or state can race and corrupt workflows. Botpress’s write surface is not explicit, so this is not high, but the shared mutable state makes conflict plausible.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or datastore
IF Botpress package installation mutates a shared runtime used by Flowise
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and datastores
Run each agent in separate containers
Freeze package installation in shared environments
Add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise’s graph-based tool nodes can produce outputs that downstream steps treat as authoritative, and Botpress is a support agent likely to render or act on those outputs. If Botpress consumes Flowise results without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect customer-facing actions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Botpress uses Flowise-generated text as final answers or action inputs
IF no verification step checks Flowise outputs before Botpress acts
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Botpress uses Flowise outputs
Require citations or structured schemas from Flowise
Log and sample-check downstream actions
Limit Flowise outputs to suggestions, not commands

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support system and Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs plus model-provider keys and tool credentials. If support transcripts or regulated data are routed through Flowise, retention and residency obligations can diverge from Botpress handling. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a compliance-gap risk rather than high.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts contain regulated personal data
IF Flowise retention or logging differs from Botpress policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into Flowise
Align retention settings across both systems
Disable logging of sensitive fields in Flowise
Review residency and DPA requirements before deployment
